analysis.reason: The deterministic mock ignores natural-language prompt instructions and returns the same extractive output for A, B, and C. Metric equality is an adapter limitation, not evidence that the prompts are equivalent for a real language model.
analysis.best_prompt_by_metric: A, B, and C tie on each metric under the deterministic mock; this is not a prompt-performance winner.
analysis.structured_prompt_evidence_discipline: Not measurable with this mock; no claim that C improves real model evidence discipline.
analysis.statistical_significance: Not assessed; 12 synthetic questions and a deterministic adapter are inadequate for inferential claims.

limitations: The 12-question corpus and PDFs are synthetic development data, not official regulations.
No live OpenAI generation was run; credentials and live service behavior were not exercised.
The deterministic mock does not process prompt text, so A/B/C output equality is expected and cannot establish model prompt effects.
The local embedding substitute is not text-embedding-3-small; production embedding performance is unverified.
Token usage is unavailable for the mock and remains null; no pricing snapshot is configured, so estimated API cost remains null.
Measured generation latency is local adapter execution time and is not representative of model latency.
No held-out dataset or statistical significance analysis is available.
